h1.text: Ship your Wix orders with your own Stamps.com account. No paid connector in between.

x1.text: Lots of online shops build their store on Wix, and print their shipping labels in Stamps.com.

x2.text: But the two don't talk to each other. Wix has no built-in connection to Stamps.com, and Stamps.com doesn't list Wix among the stores it imports orders from.

g1.text: So every order has to get from Wix into Stamps.com somehow, and every tracking number has to find its way back.

a1.text: Today, the options cost money, or time.

a2.text: A shipping platform like ShipStation connects to Wix, but it's another monthly subscription, and you print your labels there instead.

a3.text: Another store platform can act as a go-between, with its own plan, and a paid Stamps.com app on top.

a4.text: Or you retype every address by hand, and copy every tracking number back.

i1.text: Ship by File takes a different route. Stamps.com already imports orders from a file, and exports printed labels to a file.

i2.text: The app writes the first file, and reads the second.

s1.text: You set it up once. Upload the sample file from Stamps.com, and the app keeps its columns exactly as they are.

s2.text: Each column is matched to a Wix field from a fixed list. Anything it doesn't recognise, you choose yourself.

s3.text: Then pick the date to start from, so older orders are never sent.

t1.text: Each morning, the To ship tab lists every paid order waiting to go out.

t2.text: One click downloads the file. Import it into Stamps.com, and print your labels the way you always do.

u1.text: At the end of the day, export your print history from Stamps.com, and upload it here.

u2.text: The app matches each tracking number to its order, and skips anything already shipped, cancelled, or unpaid.

u3.text: Confirm, and your orders are marked as shipped, with tracking.

c1.text: No subscription, nothing to host, and your Stamps.com routine stays the same. Ship by File is free.
